 The forces under Donald Trump’s command have put their feet up this weekend. It has been two days since America launched new strikes against Iran, following 13 nights of back-and-forth attacks. The calm may not last. On Friday Mr Trump was threatening a return to full-scale war.

Hi Oleg,

Some of tech’s biggest names are building empires this week. Let's get into it:

- Anthropic has spun out a $1.5B “AI implementation” company to deploy engineers to customers’ offices. It’s a joint venture with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, and others.¹
- Databricks is set to close a $3B Series M led by Coatue, according to The Wall Street Journal. The round values the company at an estimated $188B, up from $134B in December.²
- OpenAI announced that 10M people now use its Codex and ChatGPT Work agents, nearly doubling usage from earlier this month. That’s on top of ChatGPT’s 900M weekly users.³
- Stripe’s revenue ($6.8B) and free cash flow ($3.2B) both jumped significantly last year, according to The Information. The growth will reportedly fuel an “acquisition hunt.”⁴

These reports don’t imply specific results for investors with exposure to these companies via StartEngine Private. Past performance is not indicative of future results. Additionally, there's no guarantee that revenue, funding, or valuation will continue to grow for these companies, or that they’ll be profitable.

There’s a theme hiding in this week's headlines.

While these companies are all still private (for now), they’re hardly scrappy startups anymore. They’re using billions in revenue and funding to build significant momentum.

It's a reminder that a company can do a lot of growing up before it ever goes public, and that the earliest chapters happen well out of public view.
